az_thumbelina_boulder.blurb: A single small boulder in the Linda Vista bouldering zone on the northwest flank of the Santa Catalina Mountains, outside Tucson. It is the first block you meet when walking in, so it suits a quick session. Eight problems run from easy up to the V4 range, with plenty in the V0 to V2 bracket, which makes it friendly for newer boulderers. The sides lean back and are sloping, while the tallest face is vertical. Expect little crimps and flaky patches mixed with quartz crystals, and bring pads since a few starts sit in a pit beneath a small roof. The wider Linda Vista area is known for short, low-commitment outings.

az_swamp_boulder.blurb: One imposing block at the lower end of Secret Gully, in the Windy Ridge sector of Mount Lemmon's Catalina Highway climbing. Eight boulder problems span a wide range, from easy V1s through mid-grade lines up to V8 and V9 testpieces; one of those hard ones stood as among the toughest in Tucson for years. The tall, committing lines include a highball with crystal holds. Rails and slopers dominate the harder moves, with a stream bed running right beneath the rock. Landings call for careful pad placement, and topping out onto the slab above can be scrappy, so many climbers jump off instead. You reach it by walking down the gully past a big boulder and a few slabs.

az_black_hole_wall.blurb: A small sport wall within The Observatory, a cliff band on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalinas near Tucson. Eight bolted lines run from about 5.8 up to the low 5.11 range, with a handful in the 5.10 bracket, so it works for steady intermediates. The terrain is mostly vertical, and a dark streak marks the middle of the wall where the uphill trail arrives. Watch for loose rock and wear a helmet. The cliff band it belongs to stays shaded until mid to late afternoon, which keeps it usable much of the year, though summer outings are best started early. A 60 m rope covers the routes on the Observatory generally.

az_flagtop_ridge.blurb: A remote set of west-facing cliffs high on a ridge in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, northeast of the Isle of Ewe campground. The walls can be spotted from the main dirt road, but they vanish as you draw nearer, so take a bearing before setting off. The approach is a real hike: a cow tank, a saddle, then down into a canyon creek and back up. Eight traditional lines sit mostly at 5.9 and 5.10, with chimney systems among the features. Expect a backcountry feel, with few visitors and no quick escape.

az_hawk_rock.blurb: A compact west-facing crag below the Windy Point overlook on Mount Lemmon's Catalina Highway, in the Windy Point West zone. Eight lines split evenly between bolted and gear-protected climbing, running from 5.9 to 5.12, with most in the 5.10 range. Routes are around 50 feet and the stone is mostly sound, though a large flake on the right side deserves caution. The face stays shaded until early afternoon. Older 5.9s here feel stiffer than modern ones. Getting in from the overlook lot takes only a short walk south and a descent westward, so it fits a quick half-day.
